## Problem statement

Between the 24 h window anchored on 2026-10-18/19 and the window anchored on 2026-10-20/21, logged (paid-serving) token volume rose **+96%** (421.7 M → 828.5 M) while requests *fell* 29% (12,810 → 9,137) — i.e. ≈32.9 k → ≈90.7 k tokens per request (≈2.8×). Nothing owns that trend: the verification item that surfaced it (LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO) could only show the off-peak low-priority fallback epic did **not** cause it. Until the growth is attributed, we cannot tell an intended context-growth change from a context-budget/compaction regression or a token-accounting artefact, and we have no standing metric that would have flagged it.

## Users

- **Producer / cost owner** — needs to know whether paid-serving spend doubled for a legitimate reason (bigger sessions) or because of a regression, and needs the answer recorded where the verification record lives.
- **Proxy maintainer** — needs any regression found here either fixed with a regression test or filed as a blocking child with numbers attached, and needs the failing mechanism named (compaction, context budget, token accounting).
- **Operator reading the daily proxy-usage report** — needs a durable per-request cost signal so the next drift is visible on the day it happens instead of via an ad-hoc before/after comparison.

Example user stories:

- As the cost owner, I want the +96% rise attributed to a named cause with numbers, so I can decide whether the paid tier is behaving as designed.
- As a proxy maintainer, I want a `provider_context_exceeded`/accounting check that distinguishes re-attribution from real extra tokens, so I do not chase a phantom regression.
- As the report operator, I want tokens-per-request on the daily report, so a 2.8× shift is caught automatically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The candidate causes (genuine context growth, context-budget/compaction regression, token-accounting artefact, serving-tier mix) are each ruled in or out with a quantified two-window comparison — `start_context_size`, `avg_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `messages` and `duration_seconds` distributions from `standard_sessions.csv` / `low_priority_sessions.csv`, plus per-serving-entry token triples (`tokens=prompt/completion/total`) and per-dispatch `routing_check ... estimated_tokens` distributions.
- AC2: The tokens-per-request increase is attributed to a named cause with supporting numbers, or explicitly recorded as unexplained with the residual quantified (e.g. "X% of the +407 M explained by context growth, Y M unattributed").
- AC3: Any regression found is either fixed here with a regression test, or filed as a child work item with the blocking relationship recorded (`wl dep add`/comment `Blocks:` / `Blocked-by:`).
- AC4: A durable cost metric is implemented (preferred) or, if deferred, proposed as a concrete child item: tokens-per-request (and per-session token totals) surfaced in the daily proxy-usage report with the trend visible across days.
- AC5: Findings are commented on LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO so the verification record carries the resolution.
- AC6 (testing/validation): Any metric or parser change ships with meaningful tests (aggregation unit tests over fixture sessions plus an `analyze_proxy_usage.py` end-to-end assertion), and every number quoted in the findings is reproducible from a committed command.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `REFERENCE.md`, and `proxy/docs/routing.md` if a routing/budget mechanism is implicated).
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Log retention.** Both windows are still resolvable from rotated logs in `/var/log/llama-proxy` (verified 2026-10-22: `proxy.log-2026-10-18_00.gz` … `proxy.log.2026-10-21_14.gz` cover both windows), but retention is not contractual — measure early or archive the two windows under `/tmp` before they rotate away (the `/tmp/cost/*` outputs cited in the description no longer exist and must be regenerated).
- **Only paid streams carry tokens.** Local and `munitoai-free` streams emit no `tokens=` triple, so "logged tokens" are paid-serving tokens by construction; free-tier share must be read from stream **counts**, never tokens. Any conclusion must state which population it is about.
- **Confounded windows.** The post window contains a proxy restart (2026-10-20 13:10 local) and the context-budget/admission commit series (`c443240c`, `f496626e`, `42f93580`, `ec5514fc`, `242d03f4`, `6999492a`, `a8b56995`) plus `provider_context_exceeded` (2,003 events) which did not exist pre-change. Single-window before/after cannot separate co-landed changes; use a third reference window and/or per-day series where a cause is ambiguous.
- **Analysis is deterministic only.** Use `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`; do not hand-roll log parsing, and do not edit log data.
- **Investigation scope.** This is an analysis task: fix only a regression that is small and well-understood; larger remediation is filed as a child (AC3).

## Existing state

Measured with the proxy-usage-analysis CLI (log clock = local Europe/Dublin, UTC+1):

| Metric | 2026-10-18 14:37:48 → 2026-10-19 14:37:48 | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 → 2026-10-21 14:44:27 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sessions / requests | 217 / 12,810 | 228 / 9,137 | −29% requests |
| Logged tokens (input+output) | 421.7 M | 828.5 M | **+96%** |
| Tokens per request | ≈32.9 k | ≈90.7 k | **≈2.8×** |
| Token share by serving entry | `opencode-go-3` 99.98%, `-2` 0.02% | `-3` 99.36%, `-2` 0.20%, `deepseek-flash` 0.44% | — |
| Local streams | 910 | 576 | −37% |
| `munitoai-free` + `munitoai` entry lines | 14,555 | 5,967 | −59% |

Known-relevant capabilities already in the codebase:

- `AnalysisResult.total_tokens()` in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` already sums `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` from the `Stream finished ... tokens=prompt/completion/total` lines — the fetch for per-request normalisation exists, but **no report section divides by request count** (checked: no `tokens_per_request` symbol anywhere in the analysis scripts).
- `SessionStats` already records `start_context_size`, `avg_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `avg_response_size`, `messages` per session, and `CSV_COLUMNS` in `reporting.py` publishes them — so AC1's distribution check needs no new instrumentation.
- `compaction_events` are already collected by the parser (LP-0MTHCTLAF00147IT), so compaction activity can be compared across windows without new parsing.
- Per-dispatch prompt size is already logged: `routing_check ... estimated_tokens=… new_tokens=… cached_ratio=… cache_state=… messages=…` (entry-level, independent of sessions) — e.g. 2,892 `routing_check` lines in the 2026-10-18/19/20 rotated segments sampled vs 7,016 in the 2026-10-20/21 segments. This is the lowest-cost direct test of "prompts got bigger" and needs no new instrumentation.
- Candidate regression surface, from the commit series above: `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (context budget/cached-ratio/prefix bootstrap), `proxy/proxy/capacity_admission.py`, `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, `proxy/config.yaml`.

## Desired change

1. Regenerate both windows (and at least one additional reference day, e.g. 2026-10-19/20 and 2026-10-22) with the analysis CLI into a stable output dir; archive the CSVs so the numbers are reproducible after rotation.
2. Measure per-dispatch prompt size from `routing_check` lines (`estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `cached_ratio`, `cache_state`, `messages`) for each window — this separates "bigger prompts" from "more dispatches per request" without depending on session boundaries.
3. Compare distributions of `start_context_size`, `avg_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `messages`, `duration_seconds` and per-session token totals across windows; decompose the +407 M delta into (a) more sessions, (b) bigger per-session context, (c) more tokens re-sent per request, (d) **tier mix** — free/local share per request fell from 1.14 to 0.65 `munitoai*` lines per request, so part of the paid-token rise may be traffic re-attributed from the free tier to paid entries rather than a per-request increase — and (e) other/unexplained.
4. Check the accounting hypothesis against `provider_context_exceeded` (2,003 events): confirm each event maps to at most one stream's token triple and that no tokens are counted twice or re-attributed from the free tier.
5. Check the compaction hypothesis: compaction event rate per session across windows, and whether post-compaction prompts grew (i.e. compaction shrinking less or being bypassed).
6. Write the verdict into a comment on LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO with the decomposition table; fix or file the regression (AC3).
7. **Preferred AC4 implementation**: add a tokens-per-request (and total/median per-session token) metric to the analysis report — an `AnalysisResult`/report addition plus a `## Cost / token volume` style section and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — Needs a tokens-per-request aggregate (total input+output ÷ request count) and per-window token trend helper.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — Needs the report section rendering the token-volume / tokens-per-request metric and the CSV columns it depends on.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — Needs CLI wiring only if the metric is exposed as a flag/output.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` — Needs unit tests for the new aggregate plus an end-to-end report assertion on fixture logs.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` — Needs the new metric documented.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` / `proxy/config.yaml` — Only if the cause lands in context budget, cached-ratio prefix credit or compaction handling; fix + regression test under `proxy/tests/`.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — Only if a routing/budget mechanism is implicated.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO** — *Verify off-peak low-priority fallback in a live window* (completed): the verification that surfaced the trend; AC5 requires the resolution be recorded there.
- **LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX** — off-peak low-priority fallback epic (the change the verification was testing; not the cause, but the baseline window definition comes from it).
- **LP-0MVF9N3BV00155RI** — *F4: Docs and observability* — introduced the `provider_context_exceeded` observability whose accounting is candidate cause 3.
- **LP-0MVF9N2QL001CDA7** / **LP-0MVF9MY0W002J2N3** — `max_context_tokens` gate implementation and per-entry context-limit tests: the context-budget surface that candidate cause 2 may implicate.
- **LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ** — *Design experiment: validate session compaction gains without quality loss* — relevant to the compaction hypothesis (whether compaction shrinks prompts efficiently).
- **LP-0MTC87GBV0031F4B** — *Analyze session context-size distributions from 2026-08-24→26 reports* (completed): direct precedent for AC1 — median/mean/p90/p95/max of session context sizes plus breach counts and trend analysis. Reuse its method rather than inventing one.
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** — *Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File* (completed): relevant to the accounting-artefact hypothesis — a logging gap would distort logged-token volume.
- **Potentially related docs:** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `docs/dev/cached-ratio-prefix-credit.md`, `docs/dev/contention-queue-lease-retention.md`.

Changes that landed inside the post window (verified commit → item mapping):

| Commit | Work item | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `c443240c` | LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ | Prefill-ETA admission guard: stop starting local work that cannot finish in budget |
| `f496626e` | LP-0MVGDUVS6003T2IX | Re-widen local size gates only once cache warmth is proven (capacity-gated) |
| `42f93580` | LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ | Serialise local prefills so one prefill at a time gets the full GPU |
| `ec5514fc` | LP-0MVGGI4Y0003K4AZ | Increase `munitoai-free` `rate_limit_rpm` to 3 (tier-mix candidate) |
| `242d03f4` | LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95 | Raise local warm-context routing cap 100K → 120K (and the economic-ceiling ratio) |
| `6999492a` | LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV | Second-turn `cached_ratio` scored 0.00 after a successful cold first local turn |
| `a8b56995` | LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP | Local dispatch starves returning sessions: contention queue causes local↔remote churn |

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** – Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File (completed)
- **LP-0MTC87GBV0031F4B** – Analyze session context-size distributions from 2026-08-24→26 reports (completed)
- **LP-0MSNM9BDV007DQXB** – Wire /admin/sessions to index-backed listing (bounded) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+138 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+138 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+138 more)

> Triage of the automated section: the three work items are legitimate (listed above); the three repository "matches" are false positives — they match boilerplate AC tokens (`ac1`…`ac5`) inside a calibration dataset, not this item's subject. Full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-LP-0MVIAEARO0001O7R.md`.

## Evidence commands

```bash
# both windows, regenerated and archived (the /tmp/cost/* copies from the discovery pass are gone)
for w in "2026-10-18 14:37:48|2026-10-19 14:37:48|base24" \
         "2026-10-19 14:44:27|2026-10-20 14:44:27|ref24" \
         "2026-10-20 14:44:27|2026-10-21 14:44:27|post24"; do
  IFS='|' read -r s e name <<<"$w"
  python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
    --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "$s" --end "$e" --output-dir "$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/$name"
done

# context/message distributions per window
python3 - <<'PY'
import csv, statistics as s
for name in ("base24", "ref24", "post24"):
    p = f"/home/rgardler/proxy-usage-reports/cost/{name}/standard_sessions.csv"
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(p)))
    for col in ("start_context_size", "max_context_size", "messages", "duration_seconds"):
        vals = [int(float(r[col])) for r in rows if r.get(col)]
        print(name, col, len(vals), round(s.median(vals)), round(s.mean(vals)))
PY

# accounting check: per-entry token triples and provider_context_exceeded events
zcat /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-20_15.gz /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-20_21.gz \
    /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log-2026-10-21_00.gz /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-21_07.gz \
  | grep "^.*entry=opencode-go" | grep -o "tokens=[0-9]*/[0-9]*/[0-9]*" | head

grep -ch "provider_context_exceeded" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log* | paste -sd+ | bc

# per-dispatch prompt size (independent of session boundaries)
zcat /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-2[01]_*.gz | grep -o "routing_check .*estimated_tokens=[0-9]*" \
  | grep -o "estimated_tokens=[0-9]*" | cut -d= -f2 | sort -n \
  | awk '{s+=$1; a[NR]=$1} END{print "n="NR, "median="a[int(NR/2)], "mean="int(s/NR)}'
```

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — co-landed changes.** Seven commits plus a proxy restart sit inside the post window; a single before/after pair cannot attribute cleanly. Mitigation: add reference windows and a per-day trend; if attribution stays ambiguous, AC2's "unexplained with residual" branch is the honest outcome.
- **Risk — log loss.** Rotated logs are not guaranteed; measurements must be archived. Mitigation: run the CLI early and copy CSVs into the work-item comment/summary.
- **Risk — scope creep into proxy tuning.** Fixing every mechanism noticed would balloon the item. Mitigation: fix only small, well-understood regressions; file the rest as children (AC3).
- **Risk — tier-mix confounding.** The free-tier line share fell faster than requests (`munitoai*` lines per request 1.14 → 0.65), so part of the paid-token rise may be re-attribution rather than growth. Mitigation: decompose by tier before concluding (Desired change step 2d).
- **Risk — metric theatre.** A tokens-per-request number without a baseline/target will not catch drift. Mitigation: publish a per-day series (AC4) rather than a single scalar.
- **Assumption — "logged tokens" means paid-serving tokens.** Only opencode/deepseek streams emit `tokens=` triples; conclusions are scoped accordingly and free-tier share is reported from counts.
- **Assumption — both windows are still re-measurable** from `/var/log/llama-proxy` (verified 2026-10-22); if a window has rotated away, the recorded figures from the description are the fallback baseline and that limitation is stated.
- **Assumption — no operator-requested scope beyond the named candidates** was given; four-window/tier-mix comparison and the AC4 metric are the assumed floor. The serving-tier-mix candidate was added by the agent because the free-tier line count fell 59% against a 29% request drop; it is not a new requirement, only a fourth hypothesis for the same question.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (goal, two measured windows, named candidate causes, ACs, evidence commands) was sufficient to draft the brief.
- Assumption recorded (agent, not operator): AC4 is implemented in this item rather than merely proposed — the metric is small, lives in the existing analysis package, and is the only durable defence against a repeat. Source: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` already computes token totals, so the addition is a report/aggregate change.
- Assumption recorded (agent): "logged tokens" is treated as paid-serving tokens throughout; free-tier share read from entry counts. Source: `Stream finished ... tokens=prompt/completion/total` is emitted only for opencode/deepseek streams.
- Assumption recorded (agent): issue type stays `task` (investigation) at priority `medium`; reassign upward if a regression is confirmed.

## Goal

Regenerate the four 24 h analysis windows with the existing `analyze_proxy_usage.py` CLI and archive the raw rotated log segments covering them, **before** retention rotates them away — so every number quoted in the investigation (AC1/AC2/AC6) stays reproducible after rotation.

This runs first, in parallel with the tooling children, because log retention is not contractual (parent constraint) and the base window's rotated segments are already ~4 days old.

## Scope

No skill-code changes: uses the CLI as-is. Archiving is copy-only; log data is never edited in place.

## Work

1. Confirm each window is still resolvable from `/var/log/llama-proxy` (log clock = local Europe/Dublin):

   | name | start | end |
   |---|---|---|
   | `base24` | 2026-10-18 14:37:48 | 2026-10-19 14:37:48 |
   | `ref24` | 2026-10-19 14:44:27 | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 |
   | `post24` | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 | 2026-10-21 14:44:27 |
   | `now24` | 2026-10-21 14:44:27 | 2026-10-22 14:44:27 |

2. Run the CLI once per window:

   ```
   python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
     --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "<start>" --end "<end>" \
     --output-dir "$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/<name>"
   ```

3. Archive raw segments covering 2026-10-18 00:00 → 2026-10-22 23:59 (`proxy.log-2026-10-1[89]_*.gz`, `proxy.log.2026-10-1[89]_*.gz`, `proxy.log-2026-10-2[012]*`, `proxy.log.2026-10-2[012]*`, `proxy.log`, plus the matching `llama-server.log*`) into `$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/`, preserving the originals and verifying each copy with `gzip -t` (or `cmp`) after copy. Total is ~26 MB, so a full copy is cheap.

4. Write `$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/manifest.txt` recording, per window: the start/end boundary, the exact CLI command used, the output dir, and the headline numbers printed by the CLI (sessions, requests, logged tokens) so the parent's recorded figures can be checked against a committed command (AC6).

5. Post a comment on the parent with the archive path, the manifest path, and the four headline rows.

## Expected outcome

Four regenerated window directories plus a raw archive and manifest, so later children (and any future re-measurement) do not depend on log retention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `~/proxy-usage-reports/cost/{base24,ref24,post24,now24}/` each contain `report.md`, `standard_sessions.csv`, `low_priority_sessions.csv`, and `errors.csv`/`errors.json`.
2. Every archived segment in `$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/` passes an integrity check after copy (`gzip -t`/`cmp`), and the originals under `/var/log/llama-proxy` are unmodified.
3. `manifest.txt` records, per window, the start/end boundary and the exact CLI command that produced the output.
4. `base24` and `post24` reproduce the parent's headline figures (421.7 M → 828.5 M logged tokens, 12,810 → 9,137 requests) within ±5%; any larger discrepancy is recorded with the CLI values that differ rather than silently accepted.
5. A parent comment links the archive and manifest paths, and every command used appears in the manifest.
6. No log file is edited or rewritten in place.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — used as-is for window regeneration
- `${HOME}/proxy-usage-reports/cost/raw/manifest.txt` — window boundaries + reproducible commands

## Notes

- `now24` is a fourth reference window (operator decision, plan Q1A) so a single before/after pair containing seven co-landed commits is not the only evidence.
- If a window has already rotated away, record that limitation in the parent comment and use the recorded figures from the parent description as the baseline (stated fallback per the parent's assumption).

## Implementation outcome (2026-10-28)

**Retention had already removed the 2026-10-18/19 segments** before this item ran: the oldest retained `proxy.log` line on the host is 2026-10-20 13:10:30 (the 2026-10-20 13:10 proxy restart). Measured coverage per window: base24 0.0 h / 24 h, ref24 1.57 h / 24 h (6.5 %), post24 21.83 h / 24 h (2.17 h hole where the daily-rotation segment `proxy.log-2026-10-21_00.gz` is itself gone), now24 24.0 h / 24 h (complete).

Delivered instead, using the item's recorded fallback where a window was unmeasurable:

- `cost/base24/` — the **preserved original run** for the exact window (2026-10-19 14:37:56, mirrored at `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-20/`), copied verbatim with `PROVENANCE.md`; reproduces the recorded 421.7 M / 12,810 within 0.04 %.
- `cost/post24/`, `cost/now24/` — regenerated today with the CLI as-is; post24's −8.4 % vs the recorded 828.5 M is fully explained by the 2.17 h hole (gap-adjusted expectation 753.6 M, observed +0.75 %), while tokens-per-request reproduces within +0.17 %.
- `cost/ref24/` — `UNAVAILABLE.md` plus a clearly labelled 1.57 h retained-fragment run; **not** a ref24 substitute. AC1 is therefore met for three of four windows and unmet for ref24 by data availability (no preserved output exists for that window anywhere on the host).
- `cost/raw/` — 15 verified segments (7.8 MB) + `SHA256SUMS` + `archive.json` + `coverage-of-range.txt` + `manifest.txt`.
- Committed tooling: `scripts/proxy_usage_window_archive.py` (`coverage` / `archive` / `run-window`, JSON output) with 22 tests, plus `docs/dev/proxy-usage-evidence-windows.md`, so the archive step and every quoted number are reproducible from a committed command (parent AC6).

Assumption recorded: the live `proxy.log`/`llama-server.log` are not archived because their content no longer intersects any window; `llama-server.log*` inclusion uses the filename rotation date (those logs carry no per-line timestamps).

## Goal

Pin the new per-dispatch prompt-size instrumentation with tests **before** implementation (test-first), so AC1's "per-dispatch `routing_check ... estimated_tokens` distributions" becomes a tested, deterministic CLI output instead of an ad-hoc `zgrep`/`awk` measurement.

## Scope

Tests and fixtures only. No production behaviour change in this item — the new tests are intentionally red until the implementation child lands (documented TDD convention, see LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1).

`routing_check` is **not parsed at all** today: `log_parser.py` handles `routing_idle_admit` (which shares the `estimated_tokens=`/`new_tokens=`/`cached_ratio=`/`cache_state=` fields) but nothing for `routing_check` itself.

## Work

1. Add fixture log lines to `tests/fixtures.py` mirroring the real format verbatim (sampled from `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-21_07.gz`):

   ```
   2026-10-21 03:51:45,845 - INFO - routing_check provider=local-qwen3 model=Qwen3 estimated_tokens=40741 cold_threshold=38000 warm_threshold=100000 new_tokens=2667 cached_ratio=0.93 cache_state=warm messages=23 session=herdr-1792545542-513674-2522 chain_hold_cycle=0
   ```

   Include at least: a warm/cold pair, a `chain_hold_cycle>0` line, a line with no `session=`, and one with a remote provider (`opencode-go`) so the distribution is not local-only.

2. Parser unit tests (`tests/test_llama_log_parser.py`): each line parses to an event carrying `provider`, `model`, `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `cached_ratio`, `cache_state`, `messages`, `session`, `chain_hold_cycle`; an incomplete line (e.g. missing `estimated_tokens=`) is skipped deterministically rather than raising or producing a partial event that inflates distributions.

3. Aggregation unit tests: count, median, mean and p90 of `estimated_tokens` (and `new_tokens`) over a fixture set, the warm/cold `cached_ratio` split, and mean `messages`.

4. End-to-end assertion (`tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`): a CLI run over fixture logs emits the new report section and the per-dispatch CSV artifact with the expected values, and `summary_to_json` exposes the distribution.

5. Document, in the test module, that the assertions are intentionally red until the implementation child (mirroring the existing TDD convention used by `LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A parser unit test asserts all nine fields of a representative `routing_check` line, including `chain_hold_cycle`.
2. A unit test asserts an incomplete/malformed `routing_check` line is skipped deterministically (no exception, no partially-populated event).

# Measure memory and page-cache pressure for N=8 session snapshots

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 4.

## Target outcome

The resource cost of holding 8 session snapshots instead of 2: per-snapshot
footprint, bytes per token, aggregate on-disk and host page-cache growth at N=8,
and the system `MemAvailable` delta — with VRAM reported as non-available rather
than guessed, per the fidelity convention in
`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode memory` in the harness: build N=8 distinct session prefixes, save all
  eight (bounded by free page cache), then measure:
  - on-disk size per snapshot and total (also reported by
    `du -sb` on the run's own directory);
  - `/proc/meminfo` `Cached` and `MemAvailable` before/after each save and after
    the full set, plus the page-cache residency of the snapshot files;
  - read-back bandwidth: sequential read of each snapshot to `/dev/null` (the
    proxy's restore path reads the whole file), giving MiB/s — the term that
    determines restore cost as snapshots grow.
- Derive bytes/token per size and extrapolate to N=8 for a realistic mix,
  stating the mix used.
- Record the ROCm VRAM reading and mark it explicitly non-available/ungraded
  (the known-degraded ~0.2 GB reading), instead of reporting a false number.
- Emit `results/<label>/memory.json` + markdown table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-size snapshot footprint and bytes/token, measured (not derived-only).
- N=8 aggregate footprint (sum of snapshot sizes) and observed `Cached` growth,
  with the delta between them explained (page cache vs. written-but-not-resident).
- `MemAvailable` delta across a full N=8 set, and the maximum resident footprint
  observed during the run.
- Read-back bandwidth (MiB/s) for snapshot files, which the verdict uses to
  extrapolate restore cost.
- VRAM is either measured credibly or explicitly reported as non-available with
  the reason; no estimated VRAM figure is presented as measured.
- The run cleans up the snapshots it created and reports the post-cleanup
  `MemAvailable` / `Cached` return-to-baseline.

## Constraints

- Must not fill the page cache to the point of harming live inference: the run
  is bounded by a `--max-write-mib` guard (default sized from current
  `MemAvailable`) and stops early, recording truncation.

## Goal

Produce the measured evidence the AC3 closure verdict needs: a ≥24 h post-landing window of `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` events, with the user-traffic / audit-session split and a per-event cause attribution (occupancy / capacity / predicted-warmth), so the tracking item LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I can decide AC3(a) versus AC3(b).

## Background — the original premise is superseded by later measurement

- The scheduler epic LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG and its occupancy-aware child LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE are **completed** (commit `8b7ab7a2`, in `HEAD`; the proxy restarted with it at 2026-10-26T10:23Z).
- A later measurement on LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (window 2026-10-26 09:06 → 2026-10-27 09:06, 114 events) **falsified the second-slot head-of-line hypothesis**: 68 % of events overlapped no other prefill or decode, and `local_in_flight_requests` reached 2 in only 11 % of windows. 29 events (25 %) were "fake-warm": prompt ≈56 k, priced `new_tokens` 17–182, `eta_prefill_s` 3.7–13.8 s, cancelled at 120 s.
- The cause attributed there is predicted-but-unmeasured warmth: all 5 456 `routing_resident_prefix` decisions in that window carry `n_past_actual=none`. The fix is LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (Option D, `measured_cache_deficit` early abort), whose F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD owns the fix's own ≥24 h post-deploy measurement.
- **Do not repeat F5.** Consume its output where available and add only what the AC3 verdict needs (user/audit split, occupancy-vs-warmth attribution, per-reason counts).

## Scope

**In:** window and deploy-timestamp selection; log mining over `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`; user-traffic vs audit classification using the **same classifier** as the parent AC4 measurement (LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D); per-event attribution; a recorded dataset plus the exact commands needed to reproduce it.

**Out:** any code change (admission, deadlines, budgets, queue bounds, slot counts); the AC3 verdict itself (sibling verdict item); rewriting parent AC4. Any further admission-maths change discovered while measuring is filed as a new linked work item (`discovered-from` this item), never folded in here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Window and deploy timestamps recorded.** The ≥24 h measurement window and the deploy timestamp of every admission-affecting change inside it (at minimum `8b7ab7a2` and the Option D commit) are recorded on this item **before** measuring; any proxy restart, config reload or slot-count change inside the window is recorded as a re-base event.
- **AC2 — Parent-AC1 evidence reported.** The 22-event/7.4 h measurement (12 user-traffic) with the `progress=0` signature and the audit-load split is reported against the new window using the same classifier, so the two reports are comparable and can be referenced from the parent AC4 comment by the verdict item.
- **AC3 — Parent-AC3 counts reported.** For the window: total `reason=prefill_deadline` events, the user-traffic vs audit-session split, the hourly rate for each, and the `new_tokens` / `eta_prefill_s` / `elapsed_s` distributions — reported against both the 22-event/7.4 h baseline and the 114-event fix-item window.
- **AC4 — Cause attribution per event.** Each event is classified as **occupancy** (another session's prefill or lease in flight in the same slot pool), **capacity** (slot saturation with no other occupant) or **predicted-warmth** (large prompt, tiny priced `new_tokens`, actual prefill progress far above the priced compute), with the classification rules and evidence columns recorded. The occupancy share is the direct test of this item's original hypothesis.
- **AC5 — Conversion accounted.** `reason=measured_cache_deficit` (Option D) is reported alongside `prefill_deadline`, so a fall in one reason is never misread as the residual disappearing.
- **AC6 — Parent AC3 mapping (evidence half).** "**AC3 — Closure.** Closed only when either (a) the scheduler epic lands and a post-landing window shows zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions after acceptance, or (b) the producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and the re-scoped criterion is met." — this item supplies the measured evidence for path (a) and, when (a) fails, the evidence for the (b) re-scope proposal; it does not close the tracking item.

- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (window evidence)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` (existing analysis flow)
- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` (`log_local_eviction`, `EVICTION_REASONS` — the closed reason vocabulary)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — the post-fix window is a valid evidence window.** It is only valid if the deploy timestamps are recorded first and no admission-affecting change or slot-count change occurs inside it (AC1 re-bases the window otherwise).
- **Risk — attribution drift.** The user-traffic / audit classifier must be the parent AC4 one, or the two reports stop being comparable (AC2).
- **Risk — misreading the reason conversion.** A fall in `reason=prefill_deadline` with a rise in `reason=measured_cache_deficit` is Option D doing its job, not the residual disappearing (AC5).
- **Reuse:** LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD (F5) already measures the fix's own post-deploy window; this item consumes that output rather than duplicating it.

## Deliverables

A recorded window analysis (dataset + reproducible commands) posted as a comment on this item, with the attribution table and explicit pointers for the AC3(a) / AC3(b) verdict.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator of the LLM proxy, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard to price local prefills at the rate they will actually achieve when the other slot is busy, so that admitted local dispatches convert to a first byte instead of burning the queue budget and falling back remote.

## Background / evidence (measured 2026-10-28, 23:30-00:38 + 00:00-00:38 windows)

- The local model served 15 of 1,883 streams; 1,152 routing skips and 487 admission-guard rejects occurred.
- The guard priced a 6,659-token prompt at `eta_prefill_s=13.9` (~479 t/s), yet the llama-server's own prompt-eval median is ~120 t/s (p25 85 / p75 202 / max 763, n=229 same day). Admission pricing runs 2-4x optimistic, at p95+ of the measured distribution.
- 2026-10-28 00:28:55: `decision=admit projected_wait_s=29.9 budget_s=60.0` with `busy_slots=1 in_flight_prefills=1 eta_occupancy_s=16.0`; queued the full 60 s, the gate never freed (occupant was a cold 65-89k-token audit prompt), then fell back remote — a guaranteed loss that admission was supposed to prevent. Retry was admitted again, dispatched after 13.4 s, and local immediately entered a ~480 s cooldown (dispatch failed).
- Root cause is not the gate serialisation structure (already priced as `eta * (busy_slots + 1)` plus a measured-occupant term): it is that (a) the rate calibration is unconditioned on co-residency — decode on the other slot halves prefill throughput (the single-prefill gate serialises prefills but not prefill+decode batching), and (b) the occupant-remaining term (`admitted_eta - elapsed`) inherits the optimistic rate and converges to ~0 for any occupant alive past its optimistic ETA, leaving the equally optimistic symmetric floor.

## Proposed fix

1. Maintain a separate rate distribution for contended prefills (observed while `busy_slots >= 1` / another slot generating) and price contended admissions against it; expose the chosen bucket on the decision log (e.g. `rate_bucket=contended`).
2. Rebase the occupant-remaining term on the occupant's remaining uncached new tokens priced at the contended rate, instead of `admitted_eta - elapsed`.
3. Pre/post measurement: log admission→first-byte conversion and abandoned-queue-wait share per new-token band to prove the fix.

## Scope guardrails

- Do NOT change `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) or `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120) in this item; the ordering assertion 60 < 120 < 840 < 900 must stay intact.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A contended decision (busy_slots >= 1) is priced with the contended rate bucket; unit test asserts the bucket and that `eta_occupancy` uses the occupant's remaining new tokens at that rate, never `admitted_eta - elapsed`.
- AC2: A simulated cold occupant with 60k remaining new tokens yields `eta_occupancy` >= contended-rate x remaining; the 6,659-token / 13.9 s case now projects >= median-rate prefill (>= 55 s at 120 t/s).
- AC3: Warm-prompt admissions are unaffected (cached_ratio path unchanged).
- AC4: Post-change, the share of queued local waits ending in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` drops below the 85% baseline measured 2026-10-19/20 over a 24 h window, with no new `local_eviction_after_acceptance` events.
- AC5: Full test suite green; existing prefill-ETA, deadline, occupancy and budget tests pass unchanged in intent.

## Related items

- LP-0MVKUKF65008D5UN Conservative prefill ETA for large prompts (percentile pricing >= 20k — the band floor this fix extends)
- LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV Prefill-ETA admission guard ignores occupancy (symmetric floor origin)
- LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE Occupancy-aware deadline admission (measured-occupant term origin)
- LP-0MVKUKEU80022C3U Deadline-aware local admission bound (120 s deadline)
- LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK open: Measure whether lease_state/prefill_eta predict real local contention

## Plan (LP-0MVS8T6F4006DGG3, plan_complete 2026-10-28)

Decomposed into six deliverable children in **test-first dependency order**, plus
three `idea`-stage stubs created by the AC-coverage review (each restates one
parent AC; implement as part of the named child rather than separately — see
*Coverage stubs* below).

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Covers |
|---|-------|------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Pre-change admission-conversion baseline harness (LP-0MVS9Y7FG004QJ2S) | task | — | parent AC4 baseline (verification-first) |
| 2 | Contended prefill rate bucket (LP-0MVS9Y76R004B5M8) | feature | — | parent AC1 (bucket), AC2 (55 s case), AC3, AC5 |
| 3 | Occupant-remaining priced from new tokens at contended rate (LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ) | feature | #2 | parent AC1 (`eta_occupancy`), AC2 (60k scenario), AC5 |
| 4 | Decision-log and usage-report surface for rate_bucket (LP-0MVS9YKHL007UBBZ) | feature | #1, #2, #3 | parent AC1 (log evidence), AC4 (observability) |
| 5 | Post-change 24h measurement window vs 85% baseline (LP-0MVS9Z0GY008LCJA) | task | #1, #2, #3, #4 | parent AC4 |
| 6 | Docs and rollback for contended pricing (LP-0MVS9Z034006MFZ6) | docs | #2, #3 | parent AC5 (documented rollback) |

Dependency graph: `1 → 4 → 5`, `2 → 3 → 4`, `2 → 6`, `3 → 6`, `1 → 5`, `2 → 5`, `3 → 5`.

### Vertical-slice phasing

Every child is a minimal end-to-end slice (production code + unit tests + log/report
surface + docs where the behaviour is operator-visible). There is no horizontal
"all the parsing first" phase: child 1 lands a complete, committable measurement
tool; child 2 lands a complete calibrated bucket incl. its decision-log field;
child 3 lands the occupant re-pricing incl. its tests; child 4 makes both visible
in the standard report; child 5 proves the outcome on live traffic.

Between phases: review the next child's description against what the previous
slice actually shipped, and update its description/ACs before starting it.

### Key implementation decisions (recorded for the implementer)

- **Co-residency evidence is OR'd, not inferred.** A sample is `contended` when
  the admission-time `busy_slots >= 1` snapshot on the dispatch record says so,
  **or** another session holds a live dispatch record for the same endpoint at
  first-byte time. Both signals are deterministic in tests; no heuristics, no
  wall-clock sampling.
- **Uncalibrated contended window falls back to the solitary window** and logs
  `rate_bucket=solitary_fallback`. Rationale: the guard's founding rule is
  "never reject on a guess"; a guessed contended slowdown multiplier would
  violate it. The log field makes the residual optimism visible instead.
- **Occupant rebase is token-based, not time-decayed**: `progress =
  min(1, elapsed / eta_prefill_s)`, `remaining_new = new_tokens * (1 - progress)`,
  `remaining_s = estimate(remaining_new, cached_ratio=0, contended=True)`.
  Records lacking `new_tokens`/`eta_prefill_s` contribute 0.0 (fail-open,
  byte-for-byte today's behaviour).
- **No new config knobs in this item**; the contended window reuses
  `local_admission_guard_min_samples`, and the documented rollback stays
  `local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off`.
- **Guardrails untouched**: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) and
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120); the `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` ordering
  assertion must keep passing.

### Coverage stubs (created by the AC-coverage review)

`LP-0MVSA3WOA002NAUH` (parent AC1), `LP-0MVSA3WWI00058T9` (parent AC3),
`LP-0MVSA3X5B008ZA88` (parent AC4) restate parent ACs whose wording differs from
the child ACs that cover them (coverage review matched them at 0.34/0.24/0.36).
They are **absorbed**: AC1 → children #2 and #3, AC3 → child #2 AC5, AC4 →
children #1 and #5. Do not implement them as separate work; close each as
absorbed when its covering child is complete.

### Effort and risk

Re-estimated after decomposition (supersedes the pre-plan `Extra Small` /
0.00 h placeholder estimate): **Medium effort, 21.6 h expected (range
20.0-42.0 h, 29.6 h recommended with overheads)**, risk **Medium (10/25)**,
confidence 85 %. The pre-plan estimate carried O=M=P=0.00 h (a degenerate
three-point input) and was not usable for scheduling.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Interview outcome: **no blocking questions** — the intake brief already specified
the goal, the three-part fix, the scope guardrails (60/120 unchanged) and five
testable ACs, and the six-child decomposition follows directly from them. Two
non-blocking questions are recorded for the operator; neither blocks
implementation.

- **OPEN QUESTION (directed to the operator, non-blocking) — AC4 is
  time-blocked.** Parent AC4 requires a 24 h *post-change* window. Decomposed as
  child #5 (LP-0MVS9Z0GY008LCJA), which can only run after the fix is deployed
  and a day of traffic has elapsed. Assumption recorded: parent AC4 is satisfied
  by child #5's committed measurement record, not by the implementation commits.
  Preferred option: **keep AC4 in this parent, gated by child #5**. Alternative:
  move AC4 wholesale into a follow-up measurement item and close the parent on
  AC1-AC3 + AC5. Source: this planning session; evidence: parent description,
  AC4 vs the `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` baseline of 2026-10-19/20.
  Research: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` and
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` show no existing per-band
  conversion metric, hence child #1 lands the harness before any estimator change.
- **OPEN QUESTION (directed to the operator, non-blocking) — definition of
  "contended".** The plan defines a contended sample as *any* local prefill
  observed while another session holds a slot (prefill or decode), matching the
  measured mechanism (decode on the other slot halves prefill throughput).
  Preferred option: **co-residency (any other live slot holder)**, because the
  measured 2-4x gap is a batching effect, not a prefill-vs-prefill serialisation
  effect. Alternative: restrict the contended window to "another *prefill* is in
  flight". Source: this planning session; evidence: parent background —
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` serialises prefills, so prefill+prefill
  contention is already excluded by the gate, leaving prefill+decode as the
  observed contention. Research: `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
  (`_get_live_prefill_in_flight_count`, `_live_prefill_remaining_seconds`) and
  `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_local_gate_occupancy`).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 (plan session `herdr-1793200851-672483-3216`): six children created
  in test-first order with nine dependency edges; AC-coverage review ran
  (100 % covered, three idea-stage stubs created); effort/risk re-estimated to
  Medium/Medium (21.6 h expected); stage advanced to `plan_complete`, status
  `open`. Duplicate check: `wl search "contended"` — no completed or open item
  duplicating this scope (nearest: LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK, a measurement-only item
  on a different question).

# Feature: preference vocabulary — add `local-preferred`, alias `local-only`

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY. Depends-on: none. Depended-on-by: LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ, LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE, LP-0MVSHXTX1007D58Z.

## Problem statement

The proxy's `X-Local-Preference` vocabulary is defined three times over — a
canonical table in `admission_reserve.py` plus hand-rolled copies in
`priority.py` and `provider.py` — and its only "pin local" value is the
absolute `local-only`. The parent epic replaces `local-only` with
`local-preferred` (defer while local-capable, remote once the prompt outgrows
local capacity), but every downstream behaviour change is unimplementable
until the wire vocabulary itself is widened and the alias accepted. Without
this item, changing the vocabulary would silently break deployed herdr
workers that still send `local-only`, and the three parsers would keep
drifting apart.

## Users

- As a **proxy maintainer**, I want one canonical definition of the preference
  vocabulary so a new value is added in exactly one place and both routing
  cycles agree by construction.
- As a **deployed herdr worker** still sending `X-Local-Preference: local-only`,
  I want my existing header accepted and normalised, so upgrading the proxy does
  not break my dispatches.
- As a **sibling-item implementer** (LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ / LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE),
  I want `local-preferred` to already parse to a stable constant, so the
  deferral semantics land on top of the vocabulary instead of re-inventing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `admission_reserve.parse_preference({"x-local-preference": "local-preferred"}) == "local-preferred"`, and `parse_preference({"x-local-preference": "local-only"}) == "local-preferred"` (alias normalised).
- **AC2** Sending the legacy alias emits exactly one deprecation log line per request (level `WARNING`, naming both `local-only` and `local-preferred`), not one per skip/refusal line within that request.
- **AC3** Header lookup stays case-insensitive (`Local-Only`, `LOCAL-PREFERRED` both accepted) and unknown values / absent header keep falling back to `prefer-local` with no behaviour change versus today (LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL AC8).
- **AC4** Exactly one preference parser and one set of preference constants exist in the codebase: `priority.py` and `provider.py` import them from `admission_reserve.py`; no second `VALID_PREFERENCES` tuple, no second local `"local-only"` / `"remote-ok"` literal used for a routing comparison.
- **AC5** Behaviour is unchanged at every comparison site: after normalisation, `local-only` and `local-preferred` clients are still treated as *pin-local* by the existing choke points and refusal builders (terminal 429, never a silent fall-through). Deferral semantics remain out of scope here.
- **AC6** Tests cover the four vocabulary cases — `local-preferred` parses, mixed-case alias normalises, unknown value → `prefer-local`, absent header → `prefer-local` — plus the once-per-request deprecation, and pass under the changed-scope gate (`/skill:test --scope changed`).
- **AC7** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, docstrings, the `proxy/docs/routing.md` `X-Local-Preference` table (new canonical value + legacy-alias note) and the `proxy/config.yaml` preference commentary.
- **AC8** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No semantic change in this item.** The verdict split (deferrable vs
  too-large-for-local), the deferral path and the retryable-429 timing belong
  to LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ and LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE. This item must leave every
  routing outcome byte-identical for all four wire values.
- **Wire compatibility is mandatory.** `local-only` must never become an
  unknown value: that would demote deployed clients to `prefer-local` and let
  their requests go remote behind their back — a contract violation of
  LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL AC4 and of LP-0MVRMC1L3006F0F3's choke point.
- **One source of truth.** The alias must be expressed as a constant, not as
  string literals sprinkled at call sites; AC4 is enforced by review and by the
  "no second literal" test.
- **No client-side work.** herdr `LocalPreference` plumbing and Worklog header
  injection are out of scope (owned by the ContextHub store).
- **Documentation boundary.** `proxy/docs/routing.md` gains only the vocabulary
  row and the wire-compat note; the full `local-preferred` semantics prose is
  LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57's deliverable, so this item must not pre-empt it.
- **Scope creep guard.** Any further opportunity discovered while implementing
  (e.g. a stale `local_only` token in observability, a metrics label) is
  recorded as a new linked work item rather than absorbed here.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py:56-63` — `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY`, `PREF_PREFER_LOCAL`, `PREF_REMOTE_OK`, `VALID_PREFERENCES`, `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE`, `HEADER_PREFERENCE`. `parse_preference()` at :468 does lower-case lookup on `x-local-preference` / `X-Local-Preference`, returns `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE` for missing/unknown, and logs `logger.debug` for unknown values.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py:388-407` — `local_preference_for_request()` re-imports `parse_preference`, caches on `request._local_preference`, and hard-codes `"prefer-local"` as its exception fallback. `apply_local_preference()` at :409 compares the raw literal `"remote-ok"`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:6441-6462` — duplicate `_PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` / `_PREF_REMOTE_OK` constants and a duplicate `_request_local_preference()` doing the same import-and-cache dance with the same `"prefer-local"` fallback literal.
- Comparison sites on the duplicate constant: `provider.py:6698` (dispatch-loop choke point), `:7106` (admission-refusal path), `:11460` (remote-fallback cycle); `_PREF_REMOTE_OK` at `:9947` and `:10612`.
- `proxy/config.yaml:1925-1930` — preference commentary documenting `prefer-local|local-only|remote-ok`.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md:1201-1213` — `X-Local-Preference` table with `prefer-local` / `local-only` / `remote-ok` rows.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py:386` — `test_unknown_preference_value_falls_back_to_prefer_local` already pins the unknown/absent/`remote-ok` cases; the alias and `local-preferred` cases are missing.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` and `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` send `x-local-preference: local-only` throughout, so they become the de-facto alias-compatibility suite.

## Desired change

1. `admission_reserve.py` becomes the vocabulary's single source of truth:
   - add `PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED = "local-preferred"`;
   - retain `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY = "local-only"` as the documented legacy alias, in a
     dedicated alias table (e.g. `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES = {PREF_LOCAL_ONLY: PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED}`)
     so the canonical set and the alias set cannot drift;
   - `VALID_PREFERENCES` accepts `local-preferred`; `parse_preference()`
     normalises the alias after the lower-case lookup and emits the
     once-per-request deprecation;
   - keep case-insensitive header lookup and the unknown → `prefer-local`
     fallback verbatim.
2. `priority.py` and `provider.py` delete their local constants and their
   duplicate parsers, importing the canonical constants/parser instead; every
   comparison keeps comparing against the canonical pin-local value so
   normalised `local-only` traffic still hits the same choke points (AC5).
3. Docs/commentary: `config.yaml` preference block and the
   `proxy/docs/routing.md` table describe `local-preferred` as canonical with
   `local-only` accepted as a deprecated alias.
4. Tests: extend `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` with the four
   vocabulary cases plus the once-per-request deprecation assertion, and add a
   guard test that fails if a second preference literal/parser reappears
   outside `admission_reserve.py`.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-28)

**Decomposition decision: no child items — one vertical slice.**
The deliverable is a single behaviour-preserving vocabulary change: canonical
constants + alias normalisation + parser consolidation + the affected comparison
sites + docs + tests, landing in one commit. Splitting it into children would slice
by *layer* (vocabulary / consolidation / docs / tests), which the plan skill forbids
(vertical slices only); the whole slice is ~9.5 h (Small / Medium) and fits one
implement session. Test-first is honoured *within* the item by the step order below.
Approval pause not required (effort Small, risk Medium — not XL + High/Severe).

### Target outcome

`local-preferred` is the canonical pin-local value, parsed by one parser;
`local-only` is accepted and normalised to it with exactly one deprecation warning
per request; every routing outcome stays byte-identical for all four wire values.

### Definition of done (pass/fail checks)

- New/extended assertions in `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` pass, and the
  single-source guard test passes (see *Enforcement of AC4*).
- `test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py`, `test_local_admission_guard.py`,
  `test_local_fallback_reason_tokens.py`, `test_hard_routing_cap.py` and
  `test_startup_ramp.py` pass **unmodified** — they are the legacy-alias
  compatibility proof for AC5.
- `/skill:test --scope changed` green; full suite green at the dev-push gate (AC8).

### Implementation sequence (test-first)

1. **Red — vocabulary tests** in `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`:
   `test_local_preferred_parses`, `test_legacy_local_only_alias_normalises`
   (including mixed case `Local-Only`), extend
   `test_unknown_preference_value_falls_back_to_prefer_local` with the
   absent-header and `purple` cases, plus
   `test_legacy_alias_logs_one_deprecation_per_request` (caplog at `WARNING`: call
   `provider._request_local_preference(req)` twice and
   `priority.local_preference_for_request(req)` once on one request object; assert
   exactly one record, its level, and that its text names both `local-only` and
   `local-preferred`).
   → verify: `/skill:test --scope changed` fails only on the new assertions.
2. **Green — vocabulary** in `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`: add
   `PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED = "local-preferred"`; keep `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` as the
   documented legacy alias; add
   `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES = {PREF_LOCAL_ONLY: PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED}`; widen
   `VALID_PREFERENCES` to the canonical set; in `parse_preference()` normalise via
   `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES.get(value, value)` after the lower-case lookup and emit
   one `logger.warning` naming both tokens. Keep the case-insensitive
   `x-local-preference` / `X-Local-Preference` lookup and the unknown →
   `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE` fallback verbatim.
   → verify: step 1 tests green.
3. **Consolidate** (AC4/AC5): delete `priority.py`'s `"prefer-local"` (line 402) and
   `"remote-ok"` (line 422) literals and `provider.py`'s `_PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` /
   `_PREF_REMOTE_OK` / `"prefer-local"` literals (lines 6441, 6442, 6461) plus its
   duplicate `_request_local_preference()`; import `PREF_LOCAL_PREFERRED`,
   `PREF_REMOTE_OK`, `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE` and `parse_preference` from
   `admission_reserve`. Point **every** comparison site at the canonical pin-local
   constant: `provider.py:6698` (dispatch-loop choke point), `:7106`
   (admission-refusal), `:11460` (remote-fallback cycle), `:9947` and `:10612`
   (`remote-ok`), and `priority.py:422` (`apply_local_preference`). Keep one
   request-caching wrapper per module, both delegating to `parse_preference`, so the
   `request._local_preference` cache still short-circuits.
   → verify: the unmodified compatibility suites listed in the Definition of done
   stay green.
4. **Docs** (AC7, respecting the docs boundary): update the `proxy/config.yaml`
   preference commentary (~line 1925) and the `proxy/docs/routing.md`
   `X-Local-Preference` table (`prefer-local` / `local-preferred` / `remote-ok` rows,
   ~1202-1207) plus a one-line wire-compat note that `local-only` is accepted,
   normalised, and logs one deprecation warning per request. **Do not** rewrite
   `routing.md:1270-1275` ("Local-only means refuse…") or the per-reason
   retry-contract section — the full `local-preferred` semantics prose is
   LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57's deliverable.
   → verify: `grep -n "local-only" proxy/docs/routing.md` shows only the new alias
   note plus the pre-existing lines the boundary keeps out of scope.
5. **Gate** — `/skill:test --scope changed`, then commit and push to `dev`; the
   pre-push hook runs the full suite (AC8).

### Enforcement of AC4 (guard-test design)

`test_single_preference_vocabulary_source`: parse every `proxy/proxy/*.py` with `ast`
(excluding `test_*.py` fixture modules — `test_home_page.py` uses `"local-only"` as a
*provider name*, not a preference) and assert that every `ast.Constant` string which
**equals** one of `local-only` / `local-preferred` / `prefer-local` / `remote-ok`
lives in `admission_reserve.py`. Equality (not substring) matching leaves log and
refusal *messages* untouched — e.g. `provider.py:6551` ("…X-Local-Preference:
local-only forbids remote fallback"), which AC5 requires to stay byte-identical.
Today's exact-literal sites are exactly: `admission_reserve.py:56-58`,
`priority.py:402,422`, `provider.py:6441,6442,6461`, and the excluded
`test_home_page.py:42,208` — so the guard fails precisely where the change is
expected and nowhere else.

### Deprecation-latch mechanism (resolves the effort report's second unknown)

`parse_preference()` has exactly two callers — `priority.local_preference_for_request()`
and `provider._request_local_preference()` — and both cache the result on the *same*
`request._local_preference` attribute, so a `logger.warning` emitted **inside**
`parse_preference()` is naturally once per request. **Do not** add a module-level
latch: it would suppress the warning for every later request and hide un-migrated
clients (assumption A2). No other module calls `parse_preference` directly (verified
by repository grep).

- No deferral, no verdict split, no retry-timing change (LP-0MVSHX47F003XEIZ /
  LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE).
- Response bodies, headers and reason tokens unchanged (AC5).
- No client-side (herdr / pi-extension) work.

- A1 wire spelling is `local-preferred` (parent epic LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY AC1).
- A2 the deprecation is once per *request*, not per process.

- A5 `local_only` in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` is an observed outcome, not a

None needed: the behaviour-preservation claim is verified by the unmodified
refusal-matrix / admission-guard / fallback-reason suites rather than a prototype.

# Feature: capacity verdict — deferrable vs too-large-for-local

Parent: LP-0MVSHWL47000EVJY.

## Goal

One authoritative classification of *why* the local route cannot serve a request right now, so chain selection can distinguish "wait, a slot is coming" from "this prompt will never fit local".

## Deliverables

- A single verdict helper (e.g. `local_capacity_verdict(...)`) in the admission/reserve module, consumed by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder — derived from the existing estimator/guard decision and the local provider's configured limits, **not** a second ETA or token-estimation implementation.
- Verdict vocabulary:
  - `deferrable` — prompt is inside the local serving envelope; the blocking reason is temporal (`eta_exceeds_budget_direct`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, queue/occupancy, lease denial, busy slots, stall/cooldown).
  - `too_large` — prompt exceeds the local serving envelope: context above the local model's limit/`cold_threshold` verdict, or `new_tokens > local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` (`prefill_budget_exceeded`).
- The verdict (and the underlying reason token) appears in the 429 payload and in a dedicated log line, so a deferral is never mistaken for chain exhaustion (relates to LP-0MVNTJQVB007QWEZ and LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ).
- Unit tests for the classification table.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 `deferrable` is returned for the observed incident shape (`eta_prefill_s=31.7`, `projected_wait_s=63.4`, `budget_s=60.0`, `new_tokens=6627`, `budget_tokens=25000`).
- AC2 `too_large` is returned when `new_tokens > local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`, and when the local context check already skips the local route for size.
- AC3 Exactly one implementation is used by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder (assert by import/call-site review, not by duplicated logic).
- AC4 The verdict is observable: refusal body carries it and one log line states preference + verdict + reason.
- AC5 Table-driven unit tests cover deferrable, too-large (both triggers) and non-guard temporal reasons.
- AC6 All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and docstrings; operator-facing docs (`docs/`, `proxy/config.yaml` commentary) are tracked in LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57.
- AC7 Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes

Do not pre-empt the retry-timing contract (LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X) — this item only classifies; timing stays in `_refusal_retry_timing`.

Classification inputs come from the existing estimator/guard decision and the configured envelope (`local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens`, local context limit); no second ETA, token-estimation or sizing model is introduced (parent assumption A1).

## Constraints

- One helper, imported by both dispatch cycles and the refusal builder — a duplicated verdict in `provider.py` violates AC3.
- Verdict values are exactly `deferrable` and `too_large`; an unclassifiable case must default to the existing pin-local refusal (fail safe: never promote a fits-local request to remote).
- No retry-timing change, no queue or lease behaviour change, no config default change.
- `prefer-local` and `remote-ok` behaviour is untouched by the verdict.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — the single `local_capacity_verdict(...)` helper, the `deferrable` / `too_large` vocabulary, and placement beside the existing canonical reason-token table.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `evaluate_admission()`, `suggested_retry_after_seconds()` and `COLD_PREFILL_BUDGET_KEY` supply the verdict inputs (no duplicate estimator).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — both dispatch cycles plus the refusal builder call the helper; the verdict appears in the 429 body and in one log line.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` and the local model's context limit define the serving envelope (read-only here; commentary is LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — table-driven tests covering deferrable, both too-large triggers and non-guard temporal reasons.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — helper-level classification unit tests.

# Implementation: wire capacity verdict into refusal builder, 429 body and log line

Parent: LP-0MVSL7SDV007XVG6.

## Goal

Make `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` the only source of the classification at every local-route refusal exit in `provider.py`, surface the verdict in the 429 body and in exactly one log line, and change nothing else (no timing, queue, lease, header or promotion change).

## Deliverables

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`:
  - `_build_local_only_refusal_response(attempt, config, preference=None)` computes the verdict **exactly once** via `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` using evidence already on `attempt` (`reason`, `new_tokens`, `budget_tokens` from `_local_admission_evidence` / `_admission_token_evidence`); no reason table, no second estimator, no re-derivation (parent AC1/AC3). The preference parameter defaults so existing direct unit-test callers keep working.
  - Body: add `"verdict": "deferrable" | "too_large"` to the 429 JSON payload — additive only; `reason`, `retryable`, `eta_prefill_seconds`, `budget_seconds`, `projected_wait_seconds`, `retry_after`/`retry_at`, `suggested_action` and `X-Local-Route: refused` stay byte-identical (parent AC2/AC3).

The line names the **parsed** preference (threaded in from the call sites), verdict and reason and is emitted exactly once per refusal, not per skip branch (parent AC4). The parent deliverable's `local_capacity_verdict ...`-prefixed alternative is acceptable only if the reflecting tests are updated with it.
  - Thread the resolved preference from the choke point `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote` (both dispatch cycles) and the two `refused_local_only` branches (queue and lease denial paths) into the builder so the log line names the actual preference (parent AC4/AC5).
  - Comments/docstrings updated at every call site that now consults the verdict — builder docstring, choke point, both `refused_local_only` branches — stating the single-implementation contract (parent AC6).
  - Flip the `xfail(strict=True)` verdict assertions from the test child.

## Boundaries (explicitly out of scope)

- `_build_exhausted_response` / `_build_local_admission_reject_response` (chain-exhausted path; the "All providers exhausted" wording is LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ) and the direct free-slot local-only branch that returns the exhausted response — unchanged here.
- `_refusal_retry_timing` untouched (no timing change); no queue/lease/slot change; no new header (`X-Local-Verdict` header work belongs to LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57 if wanted); no `too_large` remote promotion (LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE).
- Fail-safe preserved: an unclassifiable exit keeps today's pin-local refusal; the verdict never promotes a request to remote.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (~6526), `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote()` choke point (~6686), `_log_local_only_refusal()` (~6506), both dispatch-cycle call sites (~10057 remote-first, ~10742 local-first, `refused_local_only` ~10931 and ~11946).
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — read-only: the `local_capacity_verdict` helper and vocabulary (delivered by dependency LP-0MVSL7QJW006OYPB).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`, `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_only_refusal_matrix.py` — flip the xfail markers written by the test child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 The only verdict computation in `provider.py` is the `admission_reserve.local_capacity_verdict(...)` call inside the refusal builder; the choke point and both `refused_local_only` branches route through it (no reason table, no re-derivation).
- AC2 A deferrable refusal returns 429 with body `verdict: "deferrable"`, `reason` unchanged, `X-Local-Route: refused`, and retry timing exactly as `_refusal_retry_timing` already produced it (no timing change).
- AC3 A too-large refusal returns 429 with body `verdict: "too_large"` and the existing `reason` (`prefill_budget_exceeded` or `context_too_large`).
- AC4 Exactly one log line per refusal names preference + verdict + reason (the extended `local_only_refused` line; asserted with `caplog`).
- AC5 `prefer-local` and `remote-ok` behaviour is unchanged (existing tests keep passing) and no promotion to remote is introduced.
- AC6 Comments and docstrings are updated at every call site that now consults the verdict.
- AC7 The `xfail(strict=True)` verdict assertions from the test child are flipped green; changed-scope test gate passes (full suite enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- Import the helper; never copy its rules (`provider.py` must not contain a verdict `if reason in (...)` table).
- Verdict is additive in the 429 body; no existing field is renamed or removed; no double header stamping.
- No retry-timing change, no queue/lease behaviour change, no config-default change.
